Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Placement 4 Special Cards 5 Goats (Optional) Overview This is a co-operative game to build the mountain and reach the summit by placing a summit card (5 Copies) at the peak (level 9). No communications allowed! Cards in the Game 72 Ascent Cards: These are numbered 1-12 in three different colors with two of each number/color 3 Campfire Cards 5 Bridge Cards 5 Summit Cards Turn On a turn, you can either play 1 card or discard 2 cards, then draw back to 5 (if you can't draw that many, draw as much as you can and continue with fewer and fewer cards for the final rounds) Placement Cards can either go directly to the right of the last card on the ground row, or placed in such a way that they are supported by 2 beneath them again working left to right on the higher row Row Adjacent cards must be of different colours, but the same colour pattern can repeat e.g. red green red is acceptable whilst red red green is not The number on a card tells you how high it may be placed, but it can be placed lower e.g. a 6 can be placed on rows 1-6 The difference in value between two adjacent cards is what you must discard, e.g. place a 2 next to a 3 and discard 1, place a 6 next to a 2 and discard 4 (If you cannot discard the value required, you cannot place) Special Cards Other than normal number Ascent cards and the winning Summit Card, there are also Bridge Cards & Campfire Cards Bridge Cards - These cannot be placed on the far edges of a row, and must be swapped out with an Ascent card by game's end. When they are swapped out, they cause discards equal to the greater difference of neighbours. e.g. if you had 5 B 2 and swapped the B with a 3, you would discard the greater of 5-3=2 rather than 3-2=1 Campfire Cards - These replace Ascent cards of the same colour, the replaced Ascent card is immediately moved up the mountain to a legal empty space on a higher row, if this is not possible then the Campfire Card cannot be played. Campfires remain and are ignored pretending the card on the opposite side is the value for discard requirements e.g. if there was 3 C and you placed a 5 so it was 3 C 5, the 3 is compared with the 5 to make 2 discards Goats (Optional) Some Ascent cards feature a goat icon. Placing one of these cards adds a goat meeple to the mountain, on the ascent card that was placed. Goats can be moved up the mountain as your turn. Goats can be on the same card, after which they move together. If playing with goats, the goal is to move them to the top of the mountain. You still have to fill the bridges and place the summit card. [Rating: 1/10] Scam. Crowdfunding is not a store. Stop backing KS/Gamefound, especially French companies.

[Rating: 2/10] Lucky Duck tried to scam me for more thsn MRSP, this will probably never deliver.

[Rating: 3/10] Loved the original Tranquility after the first play on BGA. Found this to have a couple finicky rules that I did not like. I might have tried again but I am Red/Green colourblind and it was just not worth the effort. Why are publishers still using red and green?

[Rating: 3/10] I can see how people like the puzzle of this game but it didn't really land for me and I was kind of interested in it. I feel bad rating it this low, since its probably better, but it reflects my experience.

[Rating: 4/10] I feel like this is a game that has added additional complexity and rules for no reason other than to add complexity.  The art is waaay more boring (it's basically just coloured cards rather than the gorgeous art of oriignal Tranquility) and whilst I like the bridge cards to help with achieving your goal of finishing the game I would never choose to play this.  If everyone else at the table said they wanted to play this and it was play it or leave the table I'd play it because it is still relatively quick but only for one round.

[Rating: 4/10] Ups the hand management aspect of the predecessor game, but again, I'm not that invested in cooperative hand management. I'd much rather play a competitive hand or deck management game.

[Rating: 4/10] Just not my type of game. Probably had some bad luck with card draw in my two solo games. Might enjoy it more as a two or three player game.

[Rating: 4/10] The Ascent inherits just about enough from the parent game to justify keeping the name - filling in the board before placing a final tile, and difference-based costs for adjacent placements - although how "tranquillity" fits into it thematically is as mysterious as ever. Instead of a line you are filling a triangle, and instead of ordering cards in sequence you are committing to placing as many cards of the same or a similar value on each level, while meeting various conditions and requirements. [Rating: 4/10] I found almost nothing memorable about this game except that it forced me to reconsider my thinking about what types of coops I dislike. I usually say that I don't like committee coops, and so playing this game with no communication about our hands should have made me like it at least a little bit. I sure didn't, though.  [1 play]
